purpose: Development-only real-human evidence for whole-body movement and deformation decisions. Sources constrain observable motion, coordination, load paths and surface continuity; they are not geometry to copy.
rules: No source is production content or permission to copy a person's geometry, texture or identity.
A source supports only its listed permissible conclusions.
Population averages are not universal constants; preserve measured variation and stated uncertainty.
Do not infer a fixed scapulohumeral ratio across the full elevation arc.
Visual plausibility requires multiple people or cohorts where available and cannot be established from one body alone.
Evidence supports movement/deformation rules, not a single universal set of joint angles or body proportions.

source.license_use_note: Link and derived observations only for development review; do not redistribute article media beyond its stated terms.

diversity.notes: Seven men and five women without shoulder abnormality, ages 22-41; small and age-limited cohort, with three right and nine left shoulders tested.

entries.uncertainty: Invasive but small cohort; controlled planar motion is not identical to free exercise motion, and values should not be treated as one universal ratio.

source.license_use_note: Inspect hosted supplementary video as development reference only; do not copy or redistribute participant imagery.

diversity.notes: Healthy cohort of 15 women and 15 men, mean age 41.6 years (SD 10.3); the demonstration video does not itself show every participant.

entries.uncertainty: Passive clinical measurement at 45 degrees abduction is not loaded exercise; use it to reject discontinuities, not to prescribe exact muscle bulges.

source.citation: Shimawaki et al. (2019), Measurement of Flexion Angle of the Finger Joint during Cylinder Gripping Using a Three-Dimensional Bone Model Built by X-Ray Computed Tomography, PMCID PMC6339738.
source.license_use_note: CC BY article; use here remains observation-only and development-only. Do not copy subject geometry or imagery into the character.

diversity.notes: Ten healthy Japanese men aged 21-25. Narrow demographic and static CT task; useful for joint-angle/object-diameter relationships, not a universal hand shape.

derived_observations: Smaller cylinder diameters require greater flexion across the finger joints.
For the smallest 10 mm cylinder, PIP flexion is substantially greater than DIP and MP flexion; joint contributions are not a uniform curl copied across every segment.
Finger contribution changes with object diameter, so one fixed per-finger curl recipe is not a general power-grip model.
The study used five-digit power grip with the thumb opposing the fingers and the wrist constrained near neutral.
entries.uncertainty: Thumb joint angles were not quantified because thumb placement varied markedly between individuals. The cohort is small and young; use as a kinematic constraint, not an exact universal target.

source.citation: Sathian et al. (2018), Thumbs up: movements made by the thumb are smoother and larger than fingers in finger-thumb opposition tasks, PMCID PMC6196073.
source.license_use_note: Use derived kinematic observations only for development review; do not transfer subject-specific geometry.

diversity.notes: Eight healthy young adults, four male and four female. Opposition task is not a loaded bar grip, so use only for thumb-versus-finger movement character.

derived_observations: Thumb motion contributes substantially to opposition rather than behaving as a passive fifth finger.
Thumb trajectories are larger and smoother than finger trajectories in the tested opposition task.
Grip validation should therefore inspect thumb opposition separately from the four-finger flexion chain.
entries.uncertainty: Simple opposition task, not loaded cylindrical grip; combine with grip-specific evidence before defining equipment contact.

source.citation: Polovinets et al. (2018), Force transmission through the wrist during performance of push-ups on a hyperextended and a neutral wrist, PMID 28684196.
source.license_use_note: Citation and derived observations only; no article media redistribution.

diversity.notes: Fourteen volunteers; study compares neutral and hyperextended wrist push-up styles. Use for force-path and alignment constraints, not exact skin shape.

observable_landmarks: capitate relative to ground reaction force
derived_observations: Ground-reaction force transmission changes materially between neutral and hyperextended wrist push-ups.
With wrist hyperextension, force travels more dorsally over a wider area and more ulnarly than in the neutral-wrist condition.
The hand-wrist-forearm relationship should therefore be validated as a coherent load path, not just as a visually plausible hand angle.
entries.uncertainty: The study informs kinetics and gross alignment, not a single ideal exercise prescription or exterior surface contour.

source.citation: Daly et al. (2018), Effect of Push-Up Position on Wrist Joint Pressures in the Intact Wrist and Following Scapholunate Interosseous Ligament Sectioning, PMID 29157783.
source.license_use_note: Citation and derived observations only; cadaver data constrain loading behaviour but are not surface-shape reference material.

diversity.notes: Eight fresh cadaveric wrists. Useful for contact-pressure consequences of extension, not living-surface appearance.

derived_observations: Loaded wrist extension significantly increases peak pressure in the radioscaphoid fossa.
Moving into extension shifts pressure centroids dorsally, reinforcing that a push-up wrist should be modelled as a real loaded joint configuration rather than an arbitrary hand rotation.
entries.uncertainty: Cadaveric static loading; do not use to infer muscle activation, pain, or a unique healthy-wrist surface shape.

source.citation: Age and gender related neuromuscular changes in trunk flexion-extension, PMCID PMC4326518.
source.license_use_note: Use kinematic/coordination observations only for development review; do not redistribute participant media or infer identity-specific anatomy.

diversity.notes: Twenty-four younger and twenty-five older healthy adults, with both sexes represented. Age-related differences mean the project should use the coordination pattern as a range, not one universal waveform.

derived_observations: Trunk flexion-extension is shared between lumbar spine and hip rather than being a single rigid torso hinge.
Half-flexion, full-flexion and return are distinct mechanical states and should be sampled rather than validating only endpoints.
Age and sex affect measured strategies, so exact partitioning between hip and spine should not be treated as universal.
entries.uncertainty: Skin-mounted sensors and standardized flexion task do not define exterior soft-tissue shape; use for coordination and timing only.

source.citation: Kinematics of the lumbar spine in trunk rotation: in vivo three-dimensional analysis using magnetic resonance imaging, PMCID PMC2223353.
source.license_use_note: Use derived in-vivo motion observations only; do not transfer subject geometry or imaging data into the model.

diversity.notes: Ten healthy adults, six men and four women, ages 23-31. Small young cohort; segmental values constrain plausibility but are not a universal prescription.

derived_observations: Lumbar axial rotation is distributed across multiple segments rather than occurring as one large rigid twist at a single joint.
At 45 degrees of trunk rotation, each lumbar segment contributes only a small portion of the total motion.
Validation should therefore reject a single-waist swivel that leaves the remaining trunk rigid.
entries.uncertainty: MRI posture is controlled and slow, not loaded athletic rotation; use for distributed segmental-motion plausibility.

source.citation: Relationship among the COM Motion, the Lower Extremity and the Trunk during the Squat, PMCID PMC11307177.
source.license_use_note: Use joint/COM relationships as development constraints only; no participant geometry or imagery enters production.

diversity.notes: Twenty-six healthy young adults. The task is a parallel squat, so deep-squat extremes and loaded barbell strategies require additional evidence.

derived_observations: Squat depth depends on coordinated knee and ankle motion rather than knee flexion alone.
Hip, knee and ankle motions all contribute to anterior-posterior COM control.
The ankle can reach its maximum angle before the other joints, so a perfectly synchronized three-joint hinge is not required or desirable.
entries.uncertainty: Young healthy cohort and parallel-squat task; use coordination relationships, not exact target angles for every squat style.

source.citation: Biomechanical Analysis of the Anterior Lunge During 4 External-Load Conditions, PMCID PMC3396296.
source.license_use_note: Use kinematic/kinetic relationships for development-only review; no participant imagery or geometry is production content.

diversity.notes: Sixteen recreationally active college-aged adults, eight men and eight women. Young cohort; external-load findings should be treated as exercise-specific tendencies.

derived_observations: The forward lunge has substantial knee excursion but is kinetically hip-extensor dominant.
Increasing external load changes hip and ankle work more than knee work while peak flexion angles can remain similar.
A believable lunge therefore needs coherent hip-knee-ankle load sharing, not just a visually deep front-knee bend.
entries.uncertainty: Sagittal emphasis and young healthy sample; frontal/transverse control and other lunge styles require separate evidence.

source.citation: In Vivo Healthy Knee Kinematics during Dynamic Full Flexion, PMCID PMC3591185.
source.license_use_note: Use derived healthy-knee motion observations only; do not copy imaging-derived bone geometry.

diversity.notes: Five healthy men aged 28-30. Very small and narrow cohort; useful for dynamic full-flexion behaviour, not a universal knee template.

derived_observations: Healthy deep knee flexion includes coupled femoral translation/rotation relative to the tibia rather than a pure hinge.
Deep-flexion validation should therefore preserve posterior-knee clearance and changing condylar/patellar relationships instead of rotating two rigid cylinders.
entries.uncertainty: Small male cohort and step-assisted lunge task; use only to reject implausible pure-hinge behaviour.

source.citation: Hip, knee, and ankle kinematics during activities of daily living: a cross-sectional study, PMCID PMC5537477.
source.license_use_note: Use joint-angle coordination observations only for development review; no participant media or geometry is production content.

diversity.notes: Twenty-six healthy subjects, 13 men and 13 women. ADL motions broaden the envelope beyond exercise poses but do not define athletic loading.

derived_observations: Large hip flexion in real activities is accompanied by meaningful frontal- and transverse-plane hip motion.
The pelvis/hip should therefore not be validated only in a sagittal squat/lunge plane.
Multi-plane hip checks are needed before declaring groin/glute deformation generally human-like.
entries.uncertainty: Activities of daily living differ from resistance exercise and loads; use to establish multi-plane movement envelope only.

source.citation: Healthy Ankle and Hindfoot Kinematics During Gait: Sex Differences, Asymmetry and Coupled Motion Revealed Through Dynamic Biplane Radiography, PMCID PMC7878402.
source.license_use_note: Use continuous healthy joint-motion observations only; do not copy radiographic bone geometry.

diversity.notes: Twenty healthy adults with both sexes represented; side-to-side differences were small but individual curves varied. Gait is lower load than some exercise tasks.

derived_observations: Ankle/hindfoot motion is coupled: tibiotalar plantarflexion is associated with subtalar inversion/eversion changes through stance.
Healthy dominant and nondominant sides were broadly similar, supporting a symmetry expectation for neutral bilateral tasks.
The ankle should not be modelled as a single sagittal hinge when the foot is loaded.
entries.uncertainty: Walking support phase is not a squat or calf raise; use for coupled ankle/hindfoot mechanics and symmetry, not exact exercise angles.

source.citation: Ultrasound estimates of Achilles tendon exhibit unexpected shortening during ankle plantarflexion, PMCID PMC8777463.
source.license_use_note: Use tendon/muscle-tendon observations only; ultrasound images and subject anatomy are not production assets.

diversity.notes: Eight healthy adults, five men and three women, mean age about 21. Small young cohort; study also highlights uncertainty in tendon-length estimation during motion.

derived_observations: Calf/Achilles behaviour changes between low-displacement high-force contraction, free ankle motion and loaded heel raise.
Plantarflexion beyond neutral cannot be represented by merely rotating a rigid foot while leaving the posterior calf/Achilles contour unchanged.
The paper itself demonstrates measurement uncertainty, so tendon length should not be hard-coded to one simple spring rule.
entries.uncertainty: Small cohort and ultrasound tracking limitations; use to require changing calf/Achilles form and load-state sensitivity, not a precise tendon-length formula.

source.citation: Three-dimensional motion analysis of lumbopelvic rhythm during lateral trunk bending, PMCID PMC5011592.
source.license_use_note: Use derived lumbopelvic coordination observations only; no subject geometry or marker data is production content.

diversity.notes: Eight healthy men, mean age about 33. Small male-only cohort; use the lumbopelvic sharing pattern as plausibility evidence, not a universal angle prescription.

derived_observations: Lateral trunk bending is shared between lumbar and pelvic/hip motion rather than occurring as a rigid single-segment side bend.
The return path is mechanically relevant and should be sampled as well as the end position.
entries.uncertainty: Small male cohort and marker-based motion capture; useful for coordination, not exterior soft-tissue shape.

source.citation: Kinetic and kinematic differences between deadlifts and goodmornings, PMCID PMC3878967.
source.license_use_note: Use joint/trunk kinematic and loading relationships for development-only validation; no participant geometry or media is production content.

diversity.notes: Thirteen subjects performed good mornings and deadlifts under specified external loads. Exercise technique and loading limit generalization to all hinge patterns.

derived_observations: Loaded hinge patterns can use substantially different knee motion while retaining similar trunk kinematics.
Hip and lumbar loading relationships change with exercise and load, so a hinge should not be represented as one fixed trunk-to-thigh angle recipe.
The model needs separate hip, knee and trunk contributions through descent and ascent.
entries.uncertainty: Exercise-specific loaded tasks and modest sample; use for hinge coordination/load-path constraints, not a canonical deadlift prescription.

source.citation: The global end-ranges of neck flexion and extension do not represent the maximum rotational ranges of the cervical intervertebral joints in healthy adults, PMCID PMC8145792.
source.license_use_note: Use segmental-motion observations only for development review; fluoroscopy images and subject anatomy are not production assets.

diversity.notes: Thirty-three healthy adults, 21 men and 12 women, mostly young adults. Segmental variability is substantial and should be preserved as a range rather than one rigid neck curve.

derived_observations: Cervical motion is distributed across multiple segments rather than behaving as one rigid neck hinge.
For roughly half of measured joints, maximum segmental rotation occurred before the global end-range position.
Intermediate neck frames therefore matter: endpoint-only validation can miss non-human segmental timing.
entries.uncertainty: Controlled seated flexion/extension and mostly young cohort; does not directly define trapezius/skin surface form.

source.citation: Finger Kinematics during Human Hand Grip and Release, PMCID PMC10296280.
source.license_use_note: Use dynamic joint sequencing observations only; sensory-glove data and participant anatomy are not production content.

diversity.notes: Twenty-two healthy adults, 13 men and 9 women, all right-hand dominant. Rapid unloaded grip/release differs from equipment grip but is strong evidence for joint sequencing.

derived_observations: PIP joints showed larger dynamic range and higher peak velocity than MCP and DIP joints.
Flexion and extension do not simply run the same sequence backwards: PIP tends to lead flexion, while DIP or MCP can initiate extension before PIP.
A believable release animation therefore needs coordinated but non-identical joint timing rather than uniformly opening all phalanges.
entries.uncertainty: Rapid unloaded hand opening/closing is not release from a loaded handle; combine with cylindrical-grip evidence for equipment-specific contact.

source.citation: StatPearls, Anatomy, Thorax, Scapula — deltoid origin from lateral clavicle/acromion/scapular spine and insertion at deltoid tuberosity.
source.license_use_note: Use attachment relationships only; no illustration/geometry is production content.

diversity.notes: General anatomical reference; describes typical attachment relationships rather than population surface variation.

derived_observations: The deltoid is anchored to clavicle/acromion/scapular spine and inserts on the humerus, so shoulder motion must redistribute its surface form between shoulder-girdle and humeral anchors.
A deltoid cap cannot be treated as a rigid sphere attached only to the humerus.
entries.uncertainty: Anatomical attachment reference does not prescribe exact exterior contour or deformation magnitude.

source.citation: StatPearls, Anatomy, Bony Pelvis and Lower Limb, Gluteus Maximus Muscle.
source.license_use_note: Use attachment/function observations only; no illustration or subject geometry enters production.

diversity.notes: General anatomical reference; attachment proportions vary between individuals.

derived_observations: Gluteus maximus has superficial fibers inserting into the iliotibial tract and deep fibers into the femur, so hip motion couples pelvic, gluteal and lateral-thigh surface behaviour.
Hip flexion/extension should alter gluteal volume and the glute-thigh transition without allowing the buttock mass to slide wholesale with the femur.
entries.uncertainty: General attachment/function reference; not a surface-shape or exercise-specific kinematic dataset.

source.citation: StatPearls, Anatomy, Bony Pelvis and Lower Limb: Thigh Muscles.
source.license_use_note: Use muscle attachment/function relationships only; no illustration or geometry is copied.

diversity.notes: General anatomy reference; detailed quadriceps-tendon layering is variable between individuals.

derived_observations: Quadriceps force is transmitted through the quadriceps tendon/patella/patellar ligament chain, so thigh and anterior-knee surface changes must remain continuous through knee flexion/extension.
Rectus femoris crosses both hip and knee, so its surface length state depends on both joints rather than knee angle alone.
entries.uncertainty: General reference; does not define exact surface bulge or tendon depth for this character.

source.citation: StatPearls, Anatomy, Bony Pelvis and Lower Limb, Hamstring Muscle.
source.license_use_note: Use attachment and multi-joint relationships only; no imaging or subject geometry enters production.

diversity.notes: General anatomy reference; individual myotendinous proportions and contours vary.

derived_observations: Most hamstrings cross both hip and knee, so posterior-thigh form must respond to the combination of hip and knee state.
The distal hamstrings define the upper boundaries of the popliteal fossa, so posterior-knee shape cannot be treated independently from hamstring shortening/lengthening.
entries.uncertainty: General reference; not a direct exterior soft-tissue motion study.

source.citation: O'Brien (2005), The anatomy of the Achilles tendon, PMID 15922915.
source.license_use_note: Use anatomical continuity observations only; no figures or geometry are copied.

diversity.notes: Review article describing typical gastrocnemius/soleus/Achilles continuity.

derived_observations: Achilles is the conjoined tendon of gastrocnemius and soleus and inserts on the calcaneus.
Because gastrocnemius crosses knee and ankle while soleus acts at the ankle, posterior-calf/Achilles shape must respond to both knee and ankle state rather than ankle rotation alone.
entries.uncertainty: Anatomical review; does not prescribe exact tendon strain or visible contour for every loading condition.

source.citation: NCBI Bookshelf, Wrist and Hand — Flexor Tendons and the Pulley System.
source.license_use_note: Use tendon-path/pulley relationships only; no clinical images or geometry enter production.

diversity.notes: Clinical anatomy reference; pulley/tendon dimensions and hand proportions vary.

derived_observations: Finger flexor tendons glide along the volar digits and are kept close to the phalanges by the pulley system.
Finger flexion should not visually bowstring the palm/finger soft tissue away from the skeleton or make each phalanx act as an isolated hinge.
entries.uncertainty: Clinical anatomy reference; exterior skin-fold shape still needs real-hand visual evidence.

source.citation: Bae et al. (2024), Concurrent validity and test reliability of the deep learning markerless motion capture system during the overhead squat, PMCID PMC11603033, Supplementary Video 1.
source.license_use_note: Article is open access under CC BY-NC-ND 4.0; inspect the supplementary video only as development evidence. Do not copy, redistribute, modify or ship participant imagery.

diversity.notes: Validation dataset used 31 non-symptomatic adults (22 men, 9 women) randomly selected from 71 volunteers. Supplementary video is visual evidence of the task, not footage establishing every participant's surface morphology.

derived_observations: The overhead squat is a whole-body coupled movement and should preserve continuous trunk-pelvis-lower-limb silhouette through descent and return.
Tight-fitting clothing permits gross segment/silhouette review but does not expose skin folds or detailed glute/groin/knee soft-tissue deformation.
entries.uncertainty: Tight-fitting clothing and motion-capture markers obscure skin/muscle detail. Use only for gross silhouette, segment relationship and movement timing; do not close local surface-fold acceptance from this source.

source.citation: Song et al. (2023), Markerless motion capture estimates of lower extremity kinematics and kinetics are comparable to marker-based across 8 movements, PMCID PMC10494994; video-frame examples for eight movements in Supplementary Material 1.
source.license_use_note: Inspect published/supplementary frames as development reference only. Do not copy participant imagery or use it as production texture/geometry.

diversity.notes: Ten healthy adults (5 men, 5 women), mean age about 22. Clothing/marker setup and small young cohort limit surface-detail generalization.

derived_observations: The same healthy subjects were visually captured across heel raises, squats and other lower-limb movements, supporting cross-movement gross silhouette consistency.
Video/marker evidence is appropriate for segment timing and gross contour but not exposed-skin fold depth or local muscle bulge acceptance.
entries.uncertainty: Small cohort, marker setup and clothing obscure detailed exterior soft tissue; use as partial visual evidence only.

source.citation: Feng et al. (2019), Measurements of cervical range of motion using an optical motion capture system: Repeatability and validity, PMCID PMC6862302; Videos S1-S6.
source.license_use_note: CC BY-NC-ND article/media. Inspect only as development evidence; do not copy, modify, redistribute or ship participant imagery.

diversity.notes: Twenty healthy young adults, 13 men and 7 women, mean age 26.8 years. All wore the same marker cat suit, which obscures exposed-skin and detailed trapezius deformation.

derived_observations: Six real-human video sequences show slow flexion, extension, bilateral lateral bending and bilateral rotation with return to neutral.
The source can constrain gross neck/shoulder silhouette and reversibility but cannot close exposed-skin fold or trapezius-detail acceptance because of the cat suit and markers.
entries.uncertainty: Young cohort and cat suit/markers obscure detailed surface anatomy. Use as partial gross surface/timing evidence only.

source.citation: Database of videos of physical exercise and sedentary behaviours (VPESB), PMCID PMC11187402; male and female biceps-curl video clips.
source.license_use_note: Use linked research videos as observation-only development evidence under their stated terms; do not copy performers, frames, textures or identity into the character.

diversity.notes: The database provides one male and one female performer per activity; 196 healthy participants validated the recognisability/effort of the video set but did not themselves perform the clips.

derived_observations: Real loaded biceps-curl video provides full flexion/extension cycles and return motion with upper-arm/elbow silhouette visible.
Sportswear and camera distance limit local biceps/triceps, antecubital and posterior-elbow skin-fold conclusions.
entries.uncertainty: Only two performers and sportswear at whole-body camera distance. Use for gross upper-arm/elbow silhouette/timing; exposed close elbow surface evidence is still required.

source.citation: Perry et al. (2021), 3D Scanning of the Forearm for Orthosis and HMI Applications, PMCID PMC8079810; paired pronation/supination surface scans and heatmaps.
source.license_use_note: CC BY article. Use derived surface observations only; do not transfer scan point clouds, mesh geometry or subject-specific shape into the production character.

diversity.notes: Six healthy participants were scanned. Small convenience sample and static endpoint scans; not a continuous-motion surface sequence.

derived_observations: Forearm surface shape changes significantly between pronation and supination rather than rotating as a rigid cylinder.
The study reports changes in wrist breadth and skin-marker spacing, confirming skin and underlying bone/muscle do not move as one rigid shell.
Because the scans are static endpoints, intermediate and return surface timing still require video evidence.
entries.uncertainty: Only six subjects and static scans. Excellent evidence that real forearm surface deforms with rotation, but insufficient alone for continuous-motion/skin-fold acceptance.

source.citation: Reichert et al. (2022), Discriminating Free Hand Movements Using Support Vector Machine and Recurrent Neural Network Algorithms, PMCID PMC9412700; Supplementary Video S1.
source.license_use_note: CC BY article. Use participant movement only as development observation evidence; do not copy hand geometry, imagery or identity into production.

diversity.notes: Seventeen younger and seventeen older healthy adults, each group 10 women/7 men. Participants wore an exoskeleton data glove, obscuring exposed skin and some local contour.

derived_observations: Supplementary video shows real healthy hands performing multiple thumb-to-finger precision grips, object manipulation, opening and return.
The exoskeleton glove makes this strong movement/timing evidence but weak exposed-skin evidence; local palm/finger folds still need minimally obscured close reference.
entries.uncertainty: Exoskeleton glove obscures skin, tendon and crease details. Use only as partial gross hand/digit visual motion evidence.

source.citation: Kuling, Brenner & Smeets (2016), Proprioceptive Localization of the Hand Changes When Skin Stretch around the Elbow Is Manipulated, PMCID PMC5073131; control experiment/figure reporting skin stretch around the elbow during flexion.
source.license_use_note: Use published skin-stretch observations/figures as development reference only; do not copy participant imagery into production.

diversity.notes: Control experiment measured skin stretch in 11 subjects. The movement increment was modest and does not cover full loaded curl ROM.

derived_observations: Skin stretch changes most near the elbow and decreases gradually toward proximal and distal arm regions.
The inside and outside surfaces exhibit spatially distributed skin response rather than one fixed crease/hinge line.
entries.uncertainty: Small elbow-angle change and skin-marker distances rather than full 3D surface reconstruction; use for local stretch-gradient logic, not exact fold depth.

source.citation: Bali et al. (2026), Rapid Design and Fabrication of Body Conformable Surfaces with Kirigami Cutting and Machine Learning, PMCID PMC13042510; exposed anterior-knee 3D scans at relaxed and 90-degree flexion.
source.license_use_note: CC BY article. Use derived skin-deformation observations only; do not transfer scan meshes/point clouds into the character.

diversity.notes: Three volunteer subjects; direct exposed-skin scanning is valuable but cohort is too small to define one universal deformation field.

derived_observations: Anterior knee skin undergoes spatially varying deformation between relaxed and 90-degree flexion rather than behaving as a rigid cover.
A model should preserve a distributed deformation field around the patella instead of collapsing deformation into a single ring crease.
entries.uncertainty: Only two static joint angles and three subjects; return timing and deep-flexion surface beyond 90 degrees still require other evidence.

source.citation: Experimentally measured lumbar skin strains during functional movements, PMCID PMC12483186; dense exposed-skin marker grid through uniplanar, multiplanar and sit-to-stand movements.
source.license_use_note: Use published strain-field observations/figures as development evidence only; do not copy subject-specific geometry or marker coordinates into production.

diversity.notes: Thirty healthy adults, 15 women and 15 men, ages 20-59. Stronger population evidence than most current exterior-surface sources.

derived_observations: Lumbar skin deformation is large, spatially inhomogeneous and direction-dependent rather than a rigid shell over the spine.
Flexion, extension, lateral bending and rotation produce distinct skin-strain fields; a single generic waist deformation is not sufficient.
Measured sex/inter-subject differences reinforce using a plausible range rather than a single exact skin-strain target.
entries.uncertainty: Marker-grid strain fields characterize skin deformation but do not alone establish abdominal/anterior torso folds or deep tissue/muscle contours.

source.citation: Imaging Two-Dimensional Displacements and Strains in Skeletal Muscle during Joint Motion by Cine DENSE MR, PMCID PMC2322855.
source.license_use_note: Use derived muscle strain observations only; MRI images/subject geometry are not production assets.

diversity.notes: Six healthy volunteers. Internal 2D muscle strain evidence, not exterior skin shape or a large population sample.

derived_observations: Biceps deformation during elbow flexion is spatially non-uniform rather than a rigid uniform shortening.
Principal shortening direction is not necessarily identical to local fascicle direction, supporting distributed shape change rather than a simple scaled bulge.
entries.uncertainty: 2D internal MRI during repeated unloaded/gravity-loaded flexion; do not infer exact exterior biceps bulge magnitude from this alone.

source.citation: Skin Strain Analysis of the Scapular Region and Wearables Design (2021), PMCID PMC8434297.
source.license_use_note: Use reported posterior skin-strain fields as observation-only development evidence; do not copy subject geometry/marker coordinates.

diversity.notes: Five healthy volunteers; useful direct skin-strain evidence but too small for one canonical strain magnitude.

derived_observations: Posterior scapular skin undergoes large, spatially varying strain during arm elevation rather than tracking the scapula as a rigid cover.
Strain magnitude and direction vary by elevation plane and angle, supporting angle-dependent back/shoulder drape rather than one fixed corrective shape.
entries.uncertainty: Small cohort and marker-grid measurements; use for distribution/direction logic, not exact production strain magnitudes.

source.citation: Soft tissue artifact causes significant errors in the calculation of joint angles and range of motion at the hip, PMCID PMC9840870.
source.license_use_note: Use measured skin-marker motion relative to bone as development evidence only; do not copy participant geometry/marker coordinates.

diversity.notes: Eleven asymptomatic young adults; dynamic multi-activity evidence of location- and subject-dependent soft-tissue motion.

derived_observations: Skin/soft tissue at the pelvis and thigh moves relative to the underlying bones during hip motion; the amount depends on location, activity and subject.
Hip-region deformation therefore must permit tissue sliding/deformation rather than rigidly binding the entire surface to femur or pelvis.
entries.uncertainty: Marker trajectories quantify soft-tissue artifact rather than complete exterior meshes; use to reject rigid skin ownership, not prescribe exact contour.

source.citation: Foot shape is related to load-induced shape deformations, but neither are good predictors of plantar soft tissue stiffness (2023), PMCID PMC9846431.
source.license_use_note: CC BY article. Use derived statistical foot-shape/deformation observations only; do not transfer scan meshes or participant geometry.

diversity.notes: Ninety-one healthy adults, 46 women and 45 men, age 18-40; strong population evidence for variation in loaded foot shape.

derived_observations: Healthy feet show load-induced three-dimensional shape change rather than behaving as rigid blocks.
Longitudinal arch flattening varies substantially among healthy adults, so the production target should preserve plausible load response without enforcing one exact arch displacement.
entries.uncertainty: Static load conditions rather than dynamic gait/heel raise; combine with dynamic arch/forefoot evidence for movement timing.

source.citation: Utility of the Pectoralis Major Index in the Diagnosis of Structurally Significant Pectoralis Major Tears (2015), PMCID PMC4555516.
source.license_use_note: Use healthy-control photographic morphology measurements as observation-only evidence; do not copy participant images or identity.

diversity.notes: Fifty healthy adult men with uninjured pectoralis major anatomy; single standardized arm position, not a full motion sequence.

derived_observations: Healthy anterior axillary fold/pectoral curvature is consistently visible and measurable in a standardized 90° abduction/external-rotation posture.
The healthy-control cohort supports preserving a continuous pectoral curvature into the anterior fold rather than a membrane, trench or missing lateral chest transition.
entries.uncertainty: Static standardized pose and male-only cohort; does not establish dynamic timing or fold depth through the full elevation arc.

source.citation: 3D Scanning of the Forearm for Orthosis and HMI Applications, PMCID PMC8079810.
source.license_use_note: Use published 3D surface-shape observations only; do not import scan meshes or subject geometry into production.

diversity.notes: Study reports subject-specific 3D forearm scans; use shape-change direction/magnitude as development evidence, not one universal surface.

derived_observations: Forearm surface shape changes materially between pronation and supination rather than rotating as a rigid cylinder.
Wrist breadth and skin-marker spacing change across pronosupination, supporting a distributed soft-tissue response from forearm into wrist.
Surface displacement is non-uniform by side, so one uniform axial twist field is not a sufficient human model.
entries.uncertainty: The study targets orthosis/HMI shape capture and does not define loaded grip or push-up surface response.

source.citation: Zhai et al. (2023), Influence of grasping postures on skin deformation of hand, PMCID PMC10695991.
source.license_use_note: CC BY article. Use derived skin-deformation observations only; do not copy 3D hand scans into the character.

diversity.notes: 111 healthy women aged 18-26, all Chinese, right hands only. Strong sample size but narrow sex/age/ethnicity range; do not universalize exact strain magnitudes.

derived_observations: Hand skin deformation changes significantly with cylindrical grip diameter and is spatially non-uniform.
Smaller cylinders generally produce greater measured skin relaxation strain across multiple hand regions.
The thumb-index web behaves differently from many finger/dorsal regions, supporting separate local deformation treatment rather than one global hand scaling.
entries.uncertainty: Only dorsal/upper hand surface was scanned and grip was not externally loaded; palm contact and loaded wrist still require separate evidence.

source.citation: Foot shape is related to load-induced shape deformations, but neither are good predictors of plantar soft tissue stiffness, PMCID PMC9846431.
source.license_use_note: Use 3D loaded-vs-minimal-load foot shape observations only; do not transfer participant scan meshes into production.

diversity.notes: 91 healthy adults aged 18-40, 46 female and 45 male. Strong population evidence for load-induced shape change.

derived_observations: Healthy foot shape changes measurably between minimal-load and full-bodyweight conditions rather than remaining a rigid block.
Load-induced deformation varies among people and relates to baseline foot shape, so the validation target should be a plausible range rather than one fixed arch displacement.
entries.uncertainty: Static load conditions rather than continuous squat/lunge/push-up motion; toe extension and heel-rise return still need dynamic evidence.

source.citation: Foot bone structure and plantar soft tissue deformation behavior in different functional positions, PMCID PMC12883456.
source.license_use_note: Use derived functional-position surface/arch observations only; do not import scan data or subject geometry.

diversity.notes: 67 participants across three functional positions; useful for foot/arch/plantar change but not a substitute for dynamic toe/contact video.

derived_observations: Foot bones and plantar soft tissue change significantly across non-weightbearing, weightbearing and tiptoe positions.
Tiptoe posture materially changes arch geometry/volume, so heel raise cannot be represented by rigidly rotating the foot while leaving plantar/arch form fixed.
entries.uncertainty: Functional positions are discrete rather than a continuous heel-raise cycle; dynamic return and individual toe-joint behavior still need separate evidence.

source.citation: Study Regarding the Kinematic 3D Human-Body Model Intended for Simulation of Personalized Clothes for a Sitting Posture, PMCID PMC8464815.
source.license_use_note: Use standing-vs-sitting scan observations only; do not copy scan meshes or participant geometry into production.

diversity.notes: 3D scan/model study intended for clothing simulation; useful because it directly exposes soft-tissue redistribution errors in a kinematic armature model, but it is not a broad biomechanics cohort.

derived_observations: Real sitting scans show measurable redistribution around waist, hips, thighs and knees relative to standing rather than rigid skeletal repositioning.

The study explicitly reports that a kinematic body model using automatic armature weights moved soft tissue unnaturally toward the abdomen and underestimated seated hip circumference, demonstrating the exact failure class the ORIGINAL-v1 coupling rules are designed to prevent.
Deep hip flexion therefore requires pelvic/glute/thigh soft-tissue redistribution, not simply rotating the femur under a fixed pelvis surface.
entries.uncertainty: Sitting/clothing-design context rather than squat/lunge loading; exposed groin/adductor detail and dynamic return still require separate evidence.

source.citation: Effects of Kinesio taping on skin deformation during knee flexion and extension: a preliminary study, PMCID PMC8883732.
source.license_use_note: Use untreated/control skin-marker deformation observations only; do not copy participant imagery or marker coordinates into production.

diversity.notes: Ten healthy adults. Preliminary study and anterior-thigh-only measurement; use for skin-length redistribution logic rather than universal exact strains.

derived_observations: Anterior-thigh skin deformation is distributed along the thigh during repeated knee flexion/extension rather than localized only at the knee crease.
The skin path between groin and femoral condyle changes continuously with knee state, supporting a longitudinal deformation gradient rather than a rigid thigh plus one joint fold.
entries.uncertainty: Study focuses on skin-marker distances and taping effects, not complete 3D muscle surface or posterior thigh behavior.

source.citation: Evaluation of tissue displacement and regional strain in the Achilles tendon using quantitative high-frequency ultrasound, PMCID PMC5519157.
source.license_use_note: Use regional tendon deformation observations only; do not copy ultrasound images or subject geometry.

diversity.notes: Ten asymptomatic subjects with bilateral dynamic ultrasound; direct regional tendon mechanics but not exterior skin contour.

derived_observations: Achilles deformation is regionally non-uniform across tendon depth/layers rather than a single uniformly stretching cable.
Load response should preserve a continuous tendon path while allowing distributed local deformation.
entries.uncertainty: Internal ultrasound evidence, not exterior skin/calf silhouette. Use to constrain tendon-chain mechanics rather than visible contour.

source.citation: Non-Uniform Displacements within the Achilles Tendon observed during Passive and Eccentric Loading, PMCID PMC4163107.
source.license_use_note: Use published displacement-pattern observations only; do not copy ultrasound imagery or participant geometry.

diversity.notes: Nine healthy young adults; dynamic tendon displacement evidence with limited population diversity.

derived_observations: Different Achilles regions move by different amounts during loading; tendon behavior is non-uniform and load-dependent.
A heel-raise/ankle model should not simply scale or rotate one rigid Achilles strip with the calcaneus.
entries.uncertainty: Internal tendon displacement rather than exterior contour; use with calf/foot visual evidence.

source.citation: High-resolution imaging of skin deformation shows that afferents from human fingertips signal slip onset, PMCID PMC8169108.
source.license_use_note: Use fingertip contact/deformation observations only; do not copy participant imagery into production.

diversity.notes: Use study-level qualitative contact mechanics; this evidence supplements, not replaces, broader hand morphology sources.

derived_observations: Fingertip skin deforms/compresses within the contact patch before slip; stable grasp is not a rigid point-contact condition.
Contact deformation propagates spatially across the fingertip surface and should be represented separately from skeletal finger flexion.
entries.uncertainty: Fine fingertip/contact mechanics; not a whole-hand shape source and not a mandate for high-frequency tactile simulation in the app.
